scope: v7.B physics replacements — forensic deep-dive on 50 combinatoric rows from REVENUE-ROADMAP-2026-05-10.md

doctrine_check.command_bridge: verified — MCP dispatchers prism_calc/prism_safety/prism_cam/prism_ai own physics execution surface; engines below are wired through them
doctrine_check.constants_source: mcp-server/src/physics/constants.ts (Kienzle kc1.1 by ISO group, Taylor n by tool class, J-C coefficients per material)
doctrine_check.duplication_guard: DuplicationGuardEngine.mustCheckBeforeCreating() asserted before any NEW engine name listed

methodology: Each row verified against canonical mechanical-engineering literature (Shaw 'Metal Cutting Principles', Altintas 'Manufacturing Automation', Stephenson & Agapiou 'Metal Cutting Theory & Practice', Tlusty 'Manufacturing Processes & Equipment'). Equations cross-checked with PRISM physics/constants.ts and ENGINE_DIGEST.md. Variability axis = the legitimately orthogonal dimension the row introduces (per Round-2 F-r2-a8-A 'combinatoric ≠ orthogonal').

replacements.old: V* = (C / Kc^0.5)^(1/n) — INCORRECT (dimensional error; Kc and Taylor C are unrelated, exponent collapses to nonsense)
replacements.replacement: Gilbert economic speed: V_min-cost = C / [((1-n)/n) · (t_ct + C_t/C_m)]^n where C,n from Taylor (V·T^n = C), t_ct = tool-change time (min), C_t = tool cost ($/edge), C_m = machine rate ($/min). Validate via Kienzle Fc = kc1.1 · b · h^(1-mc) to confirm power-feasible at recommended V*.
replacements.engine: EXISTING TaylorEngine + KienzleEngine; NEW GilbertEconomicSpeedEngine to compose them
replacements.variability_axis: machine-rate / tool-cost ratio (shop-economic, independent of physics)
replacements.customer_claim: Cut at min-cost or min-time speed validated by Kienzle power check — defensible because Gilbert is the textbook canonical (Stephenson & Agapiou §11.3, 'Metal Cutting Theory & Practice', 2016)

replacements.pair: BeamDeflection × Kienzle → max ap subject to deflection limit
replacements.old: ap = (δ_max · 3EI / L^3 / (kc1.1·b))^(1/(1-mc)) — INCORRECT (Fc depends on ap which is unknown; coupled nonlinear)
replacements.replacement: Iterative fixed-point: (i) guess ap0, (ii) Fc = kc1.1 · b · h^(1-mc) where chip area scales with ap, (iii) δ = Fc·L^3/(3EI) for cantilever (or 5wL^4/384EI for distributed), (iv) update ap until |δ − δ_target| < ε. Already implemented in DeflectionOverlayEngine.iterateMaxDepth().
replacements.engine: EXISTING DeflectionOverlayEngine (E0127) — wire from prism_calc:max_ap_deflection_limited action; no new engine
replacements.variability_axis: tool L/D stickout ratio (geometry-fixed by setup)
replacements.customer_claim: Take maximum depth your specific tool stickout can hold to ±0.0005 in deflection — converges in 3–5 iterations, validated by Round-2 F-r2-a8-B

replacements.old: Fc = JC_flow_stress · b · h — INCORRECT (J-C yields σ_flow (Pa), not Fc (N); cannot drop ap·b geometry)
replacements.replacement: Two-stage: (1) J-C σ̄ = [A + B·ε̄^n] · [1 + C·ln(ε̄̇/ε̄̇₀)] · [1 − ((T−T_r)/(T_m−T_r))^m], (2) Merchant force model: Fc = σ̄·b·h · cos(β−α) / [sin(φ)·cos(φ+β−α)] where φ from Merchant min-energy: φ = π/4 − (β−α)/2, α = rake, β = friction angle. T comes from Loewen-Shaw or Komanduri-Hou shear-plane thermal model.
replacements.engine: NEW JohnsonCookEngine (constitutive σ̄) + NEW MerchantForceEngine (σ̄→Fc geometry) + EXISTING ThermalEngine for T(V,f,ap). Composed in prism_calc:fc_temperature_corrected.
replacements.variability_axis: strain-rate / temperature regime (high-speed machining where Kienzle's empirical kc breaks down above ~300m/min)
replacements.customer_claim: Force prediction valid for HSM/Ti/Inconel where empirical Kienzle under-predicts by 15–40% — replaces ‘good for steel only’ caveat with physics-grounded high-strain-rate model

replacements.old: ap_lim = -1/(2·Kf·Re[G(jω)]) with Kf = kc1.1·b — partially correct but b coupling wrong
replacements.replacement: Altintas SLD: ap_lim(ω) = −1 / (2·Kf·Re[Φ_oriented(jω)]) where Kf = kc1.1 (N/mm² per mm width, NOT ×b), Φ_oriented = FRF projected onto chip-thickness direction. Spindle speed N = 60·ω/(N_z·(2π·k + ε)) for lobe k.
replacements.engine: EXISTING ChatterStabilityEngine + KienzleEngine; add Altintas oriented-FRF method as prism_cam:sld_altintas action
replacements.variability_axis: modal FRF (machine-specific tap test or library)
replacements.customer_claim: Stable depths at every spindle speed validated by Round-2 F-r2-a3-B dynamic-stability fix

replacements.old: RUL = (VB_lim − VB_now)/dVB/dt with dVB/dt from Taylor — Taylor predicts T not VB-rate
replacements.replacement: Two-model bridge: Taylor V·T^n = C gives T_total at current V; current VB observed → fraction consumed f = VB_now/VB_lim; RUL = T_total·(1−f). Validate via Usui wear-rate dVB/dt = A·V^a·f^b·exp(−B/T_tool) (Arrhenius diffusion) when V deviates from baseline.
replacements.engine: EXISTING TaylorEngine + NEW UsuiWearRateEngine for off-nominal extrapolation
replacements.customer_claim: Replace-this-insert-now or run-N-more-parts decision with measured VB + Taylor curve

replacements.old: h_eff = h · sin(κ) with kc(h_eff) — correct shape, missing radial engagement
replacements.replacement: Average chip thickness h_m = (180/π·a_e/D)·f_z·sin(κ) for ae<D/2 (Sandvik). Kienzle kc(h_m) = kc1.1·h_m^(−mc). Fc(t) = kc·b·h(t) time-varying over engagement arc φ_st→φ_ex.
replacements.engine: EXISTING KienzleEngine + ChipThicknessEngine; verify Sandvik formula used (not just sin κ projection)
replacements.customer_claim: Chip-thinned feed-rate increase up to 2.5× for HSM low-ae paths

replacements.old: Ra = f²/(32·r_ε) — geometric only; ignores ploughing & BUE
replacements.replacement: Brammertz: Ra_total = Ra_geo + Ra_min where Ra_geo = f²/(32·r_ε) and Ra_min = h_min/2·(1 + r_ε/(2·h_min)) accounting for minimum-chip-thickness ploughing (h_min ≈ 0.3·r_β with r_β = edge radius)
replacements.engine: NEW BrammertzRoughnessEngine — composed in prism_calc:ra_predict
replacements.customer_claim: Ra prediction within ±15% even at low fz where geometric formula fails badly

replacements.old: F = P_avail/(kc·ap·ae) — correct topology
replacements.replacement: F = (η·P_spindle·60·1000) / (kc·ap·ae) where kc = kc1.1·h_m^(−mc) (chip-thinning corrected), η = mechanical efficiency (0.75–0.90), 60·1000 converts kW→N·mm/min. Spec-sheet validate against torque curve (constant-power above base speed).
replacements.engine: EXISTING MRREngine + SpindlePowerEngine + KienzleEngine; wire as prism_calc:feed_power_limited
replacements.customer_claim: Maximum feed without tripping spindle-overload alarm — validated against measured power draw

replacements.old: minimize Σt_i(V_i,f_i) subject to Σ constraints — claimed convex (FALSE; Taylor V·T^n=C makes T nonconvex in V)
replacements.replacement: Non-convex MINLP — use Simulated Annealing (Metropolis acceptance, geometric cooling β=0.95) OR Genetic Algorithm (NSGA-II for multi-objective cost/time/quality). Avoid claim of optimality; report best-found ± standard-error across 30 restarts.
replacements.engine: NEW SimulatedAnnealingEngine or GeneticAlgorithmEngine — composed in prism_ai:cycle_optimize
replacements.variability_axis: objective weighting (cost-min vs time-min vs quality-max)
replacements.customer_claim: 10–25% cycle reduction vs baseline programmer settings (honest non-optimality disclaimer)

replacements.old: PI = ŷ ± q_α(|resid|) — symmetric, marginal coverage only
replacements.replacement: Split-Conformal Quantile Regression (CQR, Romano et al. 2019): fit q̂_lo, q̂_hi quantile regressors; calibrate with E_i = max(q̂_lo(x_i)−y_i, y_i−q̂_hi(x_i)); PI = [q̂_lo − Q_α(E), q̂_hi + Q_α(E)]. Asymmetric, locally adaptive, distribution-free 1−α coverage.
replacements.engine: EXISTING ConformalCalibrationEngine — upgrade to CQR variant; reference round2 NN-CONFORMAL03 work already merged
replacements.customer_claim: Tight intervals where prediction is confident, wide where uncertain — beats fixed ±10% by 30–60% width

replacements.old: Z3 solves linear stack-up — Z3 is for symbolic/SMT, not numeric optimization
replacements.replacement: Two-tier: (i) Z3 for symbolic feasibility (does any assignment satisfy GD&T constraints?), (ii) MIP (CBC/Gurobi) for numeric optimization (minimize cost of tightening tolerances) once feasibility established. Worst-case = arithmetic sum; RSS = root-sum-square for statistical stack.
replacements.engine: EXISTING Z3Engine for feasibility + NEW MIPSolverEngine (or pull pre-built MILP via npm) for optimization
replacements.variability_axis: stack-up method (worst-case vs statistical vs Monte-Carlo)
replacements.customer_claim: Loosen tolerances where stack-up math proves it's safe — 10–30% inspection-time reduction

replacements.old: σ_res = J-C(ε_residual) — needs deformation history
replacements.replacement: Coupled thermomechanical FEA with J-C as constitutive law; ε_residual from post-cutting unloading + thermal contraction. Reduced-order: empirical Capello model σ_res = α·E·ΔT − β·σ_y where ΔT from Loewen-Shaw.
replacements.engine: NEW ResidualStressEngine (Capello reduced-order) + EXTERNAL FEA bridge for full coupling
replacements.customer_claim: Predict warp/distortion on thin-wall parts before cutting metal

replacements.old: k = (2π·f_n)²·m — correct for SDOF approximation
replacements.replacement: Multi-mode modal extraction from tap-test FFT: identify peaks → fit each mode (f_n, ζ, k_modal) → sum H(jω) = Σ 1/(k_i(1−r_i²+2jζ_i·r_i)). Feed full Φ_oriented(jω) to Altintas SLD (row 3).
replacements.engine: EXISTING ChatterStabilityEngine + ModalAnalysisEngine; verify multi-mode (not single-mode) FRF used
replacements.variability_axis: modal density (how many lobes show in SLD)
replacements.customer_claim: SLD lobes derived from your machine's tap test, not generic library

replacements.old: Q = MRR · kc · (1−η_chip) — approximately right; η_chip needs source
replacements.replacement: Loewen-Shaw partition: heat into chip R_chip ≈ 0.85–0.95, into tool R_tool ≈ 0.02–0.10, into workpiece R_wp = 1−R_chip−R_tool. T_chip = T_amb + R_chip·kc·V·h/(ρ·c·V·h) = T_amb + R_chip·kc/(ρ·c). T_tool from inverse-conduction Komanduri-Hou.
replacements.engine: EXISTING ThermalEngine; verify Loewen-Shaw partition coefficients are used (not flat assumption)
replacements.customer_claim: Coolant-on vs MQL vs dry decision with quantified temperature delta

replacements.old: R(T) = exp(−(T/η)^β) — correct Weibull but η,β need fit
replacements.replacement: Weibull fit from historical T data; η ≈ Taylor-predicted T, β = shape (β=1 exponential, β>1 wear-out). Conditional RUL given current age t: E[RUL | T>t] = η·Γ(1+1/β)·(1 − F(t))/R(t). Update β as data accumulates (Bayesian).
replacements.engine: EXISTING TaylorEngine + NEW WeibullReliabilityEngine — composed in prism_calc:rul_weibull
replacements.customer_claim: Probabilistic life: 90% chance this insert lasts N more parts (not deterministic)

replacements.old: Fc depends on r_β — ploughing model needed
replacements.replacement: Slip-line field model: Fc = σ̄·b·h_eff where h_eff = max(h, h_min), h_min = r_β·(1 − sin(α_eff)), α_eff = α − arcsin(r_β/(r_β+h)). Below h_min: ploughing-dominated, Fc·∝ r_β rather than h.
replacements.engine: NEW MicroGeometryForceEngine — for finishing-pass force prediction
replacements.customer_claim: Predict force on finishing passes where h/r_β <1 and conventional Kienzle fails

replacements.old: BUE occurs when T_chip < T_BUE — needs material-specific T_BUE
replacements.replacement: Trent diagram: BUE region bounded by T_chip ∈ [T_BUE_lo, T_BUE_hi] (≈ 200–600°C for steel). Compute T_chip = T_amb + R_chip·kc/(ρ·c) (Loewen-Shaw). Recommend V to push T_chip above T_BUE_hi for steel, below T_BUE_lo for Al.
replacements.engine: NEW BUEAvoidanceEngine — composed with existing ThermalEngine
replacements.customer_claim: Pick V to dodge built-up-edge zone — surface finish improvement guarantee

replacements.old: Effective depth = f(pressure) — empirical only
replacements.replacement: Chip-evacuation criterion: V_coolant·A_flute_clearance > MRR·ρ_chip/ρ_coolant (mass balance). Peck-depth d_peck = min(3D, V_coolant·t_dwell/MRR). HPC ≥ 70 bar enables full-depth deep-hole; through-tool < 20 bar requires pecking.
replacements.engine: NEW CoolantEvacuationEngine
replacements.customer_claim: Peck-cycle elimination above threshold pressure — 30–50% cycle-time reduction on deep holes

replacements.old: k_total = k_tool ⊕ k_fixture in series
replacements.replacement: Compliance-summation: 1/k_total(ω) = 1/k_spindle(ω) + 1/k_tool(ω) + 1/k_part(ω) + 1/k_fixture(ω). Each frequency-dependent. Re-run Altintas SLD with combined FRF; weakest link dominates lowest stable depth.
replacements.engine: EXISTING ChatterStabilityEngine + WorkholdingEngine; compose FRFs (not just stiffnesses)
replacements.customer_claim: Identify whether tool, part, or fixture is the chatter limiter — actionable upgrade target

replacements.old: MRR_eff = MRR_nominal · cos(θ_tilt) — ignores 5ax velocity
replacements.replacement: MRR_eff(t) = a_e(t)·a_p(t)·v_f_proj(t) where v_f_proj = ||(v_x,v_y,v_z) − ω×r||, ω = rotary-axis velocity. Effective feed at cutter = sum of linear + (rotary × radius). Use forward-kinematics Jacobian J(q)·q̇.
replacements.engine: EXISTING Multi5AxisKinematicsEngine + MRREngine; expose joint-space → tool-tip velocity transformation
replacements.variability_axis: 5ax configuration (table/table, head/head, mixed) and tool length
replacements.customer_claim: True MRR accounting for rotary-axis contributions — eliminates 'feed mystery' on 5ax

replacements.old: P(in-spec) = Φ((USL−μ)/σ) − Φ((LSL−μ)/σ) — Cpk formula correct
replacements.replacement: Confirmed: Cpk = min((USL−μ)/3σ, (μ−LSL)/3σ); P(in-spec) = Φ(3Cpk_min) approximated. Compose with setup-error σ_setup orthogonal to process σ_process: σ_total = sqrt(σ_setup² + σ_process²).
replacements.engine: EXISTING CpkEngine + ToleranceStackEngine + SetupErrorEngine
replacements.variability_axis: first-part vs steady-state distribution (setup-error decays after warm-up)
replacements.customer_claim: Probability your first part meets print — quantified scrap-risk

replacements.old: Direct lookup from table — not an equation, framing wrong
replacements.replacement: Frame as RULE not equation: insert_grade × material → (V_rec, f_rec, ap_rec) tuple from Sandvik/Kennametal/Iscar catalogs. Then PHYSICS VALIDATION: Kienzle Fc < Fc_max(grade), Taylor T > T_min(economic). Lookup is initial guess, physics is the gate.
replacements.engine: EXISTING ToolCatalogEngine + KienzleEngine + TaylorEngine; expose prism_calc:validate_recommended_data
replacements.customer_claim: Catalog values verified against your actual stickout/spindle/horsepower — flag mismatches

replacements.old: δ_total = Σ |δ_i| — worst-case stack
replacements.replacement: Probe-uncertainty stack: σ_probe (repeatability) + σ_calib (stylus error) + σ_thermal (machine growth). u_combined = sqrt(σ_probe² + σ_calib² + σ_thermal²) per GUM (ISO/IEC Guide 98). Compare to feature tolerance/4 (10% rule for measurement uncertainty).
replacements.engine: EXISTING ProbingEngine + NEW MeasurementUncertaintyEngine (GUM-compliant)
replacements.customer_claim: Probe results trustworthy or re-measure — quantified U_95

replacements.old: Δz = α·L·ΔT — confirmed correct
replacements.replacement: Confirmed thermal expansion ΔL = α·L·ΔT, α ≈ 11×10⁻⁶/K steel, 23×10⁻⁶/K Al. Plus spindle-growth model from warm-up curve: ΔZ_spindle(t) = ΔZ_∞·(1 − exp(−t/τ)), τ ≈ 30–90 min. Compensate via probe-check every τ.
replacements.engine: EXISTING ThermalEngine + NEW SpindleGrowthEngine (time-constant warm-up model)
replacements.customer_claim: Auto-trigger probe-and-comp when spindle drift exceeds spec — no manual warm-up clock

replacements.old: Direct table lookup — not equation
replacements.replacement: Frame as DATA SURFACE not equation: ISO group (P/M/K/N/S/H) → kc1.1 ∈ {1800, 2100, 1100, 700, 2800, 3200} MPa, mc ∈ {0.25, 0.25, 0.22, 0.20, 0.30, 0.30}. From constants.ts. Sub-grades (P10, P20...) interpolate via hardness correlation.
replacements.engine: EXISTING MaterialDatabaseEngine + KienzleEngine; data lives in constants.ts (canonical, single-source)
replacements.customer_claim: Material constants from canonical PRISM table — no hardcoded magic numbers

replacements.old: Single equation claim — WRONG framing (it's a binary classifier, not a closed-form)
replacements.replacement: RULE not EQUATION: decision tree with thresholds (conductivity > 0.1 S/m, thickness/wire-diameter ratio < 200, kerf-corner radius ≥ wire_r + 0.02mm, taper ≤ 15°). Each rule from WEDM physics constraint (electrical, geometric, mechanical). Output: GO / CONDITIONAL / NO-GO + binding constraint.
replacements.engine: EXISTING WEDMFeasibilityEngine — reframe outputs as rule-fired audit-trail, not equation result
replacements.variability_axis: binding-constraint regime (which physics limit hit first)
replacements.customer_claim: Why-it-fails answer in 4 dimensions, not just yes/no

replacements.old: v_cut = f(I_on, t_on, flushing) — empirical
replacements.replacement: MRR_WEDM = α·U·I·t_on·η_flush where η_flush ∈ [0.5, 1.0] depends on debris-evacuation (gap-flow rate ≥ critical Q_c = k·MRR/h). v_cut = MRR/(h·kerf). Physics from Kuriachen-Mathew electrothermal model.
replacements.engine: EXISTING WEDMFlushingEngine + WEDMSparkEnergyEngine — wire to prism_calc:wedm_cut_speed
replacements.customer_claim: Cut-speed vs flushing trade-off — find sweet spot

replacements.old: δ_wire = F·L²/(8·T) — string-deflection correct
replacements.replacement: Confirmed catenary: δ = (F_lat·L²)/(8·T_wire) for transverse load; F_lat from spark-pressure + flushing-pressure imbalance. Corner overcut Δr = δ_wire when wire enters corner. Compensate via trim-cycles (multi-pass) or velocity reduction.
replacements.engine: EXISTING WEDMWireDeflectionEngine (E0554)
replacements.customer_claim: Corner-accuracy improvement via tension optimization — quantified Δr

replacements.old: N = 1000·V/(π·D) — confirmed correct
replacements.replacement: Confirmed CSS RPM N = 1000·V/(π·D); but spindle has N_max → clamp at small-D crossover D_clamp = 1000·V/(π·N_max). Below D_clamp, fall off CSS (drops below target V). G96 mode controllers handle automatically.
replacements.engine: EXISTING TurningEngine; verify N_clamp behavior at low-D
replacements.customer_claim: Honest V at small diameters where machine can't maintain CSS

replacements.old: infeed_n = (depth/passes)^k — needs k justification
replacements.replacement: Constant-load infeed (k=0.5): Δd_n = d_total·(√n − √(n−1))/√N. Constant-depth: Δd_n = d_total/N (load increases). Modified flank infeed for unilateral chip-flow: alternating + & − offset per pass.
replacements.engine: EXISTING LatheThreadingEngine; expose infeed-strategy selector
replacements.variability_axis: thread-class (UN-2A vs UN-3A vs Acme vs trapezoidal) + material
replacements.customer_claim: Thread-form quality optimized to thread spec — Class 3A holds, Class 2A optimizes for cycle

replacements.old: T_drill = kc·D²/8 — torque-from-Kienzle correct shape
replacements.replacement: Drill torque M = kc·D²/8·f_per_rev·sin(point_angle/2); thrust Fz = kc·D·f/2. Peck if M > M_max OR chip-evacuation (row 18) violated OR L/D > 5. Peck-depth from min(3D, M_max/(kc·D·f_per_rev/(D/8))).
replacements.engine: EXISTING DrillCycleEngine + KienzleEngine
replacements.customer_claim: Peck-cycle elimination where physics allows full-depth — quantified time savings

replacements.old: v_z = N·pitch — kinematic identity, correct
replacements.replacement: Confirmed sync v_z = N·pitch. Failure mode: spindle-acceleration limit α_max < 2π·N²/(z_min) for reversal — limits tapping depth at high N. Safe N_max_tap = √(α_max·z_safe/(2π)). Floating-tap-holder eases sync error tolerance.
replacements.engine: EXISTING TappingEngine; expose accel-limited N_max
replacements.customer_claim: Maximum tap RPM before sync-loss alarm — quantified per machine

replacements.old: lobe shift = f(a_e/D) — phenomenology correct
replacements.replacement: Engagement-dependent SLD: average directional factor changes with φ_st, φ_ex. Down-milling (a_e/D=0.5) shifts lobes ~10% vs full-immersion. Compute exact via Altintas time-domain or zeroth-order frequency-domain method with engagement-averaged Φ.
replacements.engine: EXISTING ChatterStabilityEngine; verify engagement-aware mode
replacements.variability_axis: radial-engagement regime (HSM low-ae vs conventional full-immersion)
replacements.customer_claim: Different stable-RPM zones for HSM vs conventional — both leveraged

replacements.old: f(t) = f_nom · (P_target/P_actual)^α — control-law shape correct
replacements.replacement: PI control on spindle-power: f_new = f_nom + Kp·(P_target − P_actual) + Ki·∫(P_target − P_actual)dt. Saturate at f_max (mechanical) and f_min (BUE/chip-load). Optionally feed-forward kc·ap·ae estimate.
replacements.engine: EXISTING AdaptiveControlEngine + SpindlePowerEngine; verify PI tuning + saturation
replacements.variability_axis: load-variation regime (varying ae cast/forged vs uniform stock)
replacements.customer_claim: Constant-load auto-feed = consistent finish + 15–25% cycle reduction on variable stock

replacements.old: δ_wall = Fc·L³/(3·E·I) — cantilever, missing axial position
replacements.replacement: Walled-cut deflection profile δ(z) = Fc(z)·z²·(3L−z)/(6EI) where Fc(z) varies with engagement depth. For finish-pass, Fc≈const → δ_max at tool-tip. Skin/skim-pass compensation: pre-bias toolpath by predicted δ.
replacements.engine: EXISTING DeflectionOverlayEngine (E0127); expose wall-profile output
replacements.customer_claim: Wall-straightness prediction with toolpath pre-bias = first-part-in-spec

replacements.old: kc_corrected = kc_base + NN(features) — generic
replacements.replacement: Residual model: kc_actual = kc_Kienzle·(1 + δ(V,f,coolant,tool-grade)) where δ from feature-engineered NN trained on shop data. Conformal prediction (row 10) gives uncertainty on δ. Reject ML if outside training-distribution.
replacements.engine: EXISTING MLPipelineEngine + ConformalCalibrationEngine + KienzleEngine
replacements.customer_claim: Personalized kc for YOUR shop — improves over generic Kienzle by 10–20%

replacements.old: T_eff = T_dry − ΔT_coolant — empirical
replacements.replacement: Heat-balance: T_chip_steady = T_amb + Q_cut/(h_conv·A_chip·η_coolant). MQL η ≈ 0.3 (lubrication-dominant, minor cooling); flood η ≈ 0.7 (cooling-dominant). Selector: dry if T_chip_dry < T_BUE_hi & no chip-evac issue, else MQL/flood per material.
replacements.engine: EXISTING ThermalEngine + NEW CoolantSelectorEngine
replacements.customer_claim: Quantified MQL/flood ROI vs dry — per material + ops cost

replacements.old: control-chart limits 3σ — symmetric, slow
replacements.replacement: CUSUM (rapid small-shift detection): S_h_n = max(0, S_h_{n-1} + (x_n − μ₀ − k)), alarm when S_h > h. Tuning: k = δ/2 (target shift), h = 4 (false-alarm rate). For ARL₁ < 10 on 1σ shift, CUSUM beats Shewhart 3σ (which needs ~50 obs). Use EWMA instead when smoother decay preferred: z_n = λ·x_n + (1−λ)·z_{n-1}.
replacements.engine: EXISTING SPCEngine; ADD CUSUMEngine variant — pick CUSUM for fast detect, EWMA for smooth filter
replacements.variability_axis: shift-magnitude regime (small drift vs large step)
replacements.customer_claim: Detect 1σ drift in 8 parts vs 50 with Shewhart

replacements.old: Replace when expected_cost(replace) < expected_cost(continue) — correct decision rule
replacements.replacement: Confirmed: replace when E[cost_continue] = P(fail|t)·(cost_scrap + cost_unplanned) + (1−P(fail|t))·cost_normal > cost_planned_replace. P(fail|t) from Weibull (row 15). Plus risk-aversion: replace at α-quantile of T not mean.
replacements.engine: EXISTING ToolWearEngine + WeibullReliabilityEngine; expose threshold-trigger action
replacements.customer_claim: Optimal replace-now vs run-more decision under your shop's cost structure

replacements.old: throughput = jobs / (Σ t_setup + Σ t_run) — deterministic
replacements.replacement: Markov M/G/1 queue: ρ = λ/μ utilization, W_q = ρ·E[S²]/(2·(1−ρ)) waiting time. Setup-included service: E[S] = t_setup_mean + t_run_mean. Throughput = λ_in·(1 − P_block). For multi-machine: Jackson network or simulation.
replacements.engine: NEW QueueingShopEngine — composes with SchedulerEngine
replacements.variability_axis: shop-load regime (light ρ<0.7 / heavy ρ>0.85 / overload)
replacements.customer_claim: Realistic throughput accounting for queue waiting — not best-case sum

replacements.old: Q* = √(2DS/H) — deterministic-demand EOQ wrong for variable demand
replacements.replacement: (s, S) policy for stochastic demand: reorder when inventory < s, order up to S. s = E[D_LT] + z_α·σ_LT (safety stock for service level α), S = s + EOQ. EOQ formula still gives order size; safety stock handles variance. For lumpy demand: Croston's method for forecast.
replacements.engine: NEW InventoryPolicyEngine — replaces naive EOQ in prism_calc:reorder_point
replacements.customer_claim: Service level target met without overstock — quantified stockout probability

replacements.old: E_part = kc·V_metal·η — power×time, correct
replacements.replacement: Total energy: E_part = (kc·MRR·t_cut)/η_machine + P_idle·t_total. $/part = E_part·rate_$/kWh. η_machine ≈ 0.6–0.8 (spindle + servo + auxiliary). Idle power often 40% of total — don't ignore.
replacements.engine: EXISTING EnergyEngine + KienzleEngine; verify P_idle included
replacements.customer_claim: True energy $/part including idle overhead — opportunity for lights-out scheduling

replacements.old: Pareto front from grid search — slow
replacements.replacement: NSGA-II genetic algorithm (Deb 2002): population evolves under non-dominated sorting + crowding distance. Yields Pareto front in 50–200 generations. Visualize as 3D scatter (cost, time, surface-finish); customer picks operating point per preference.
replacements.engine: NEW NSGA2Engine (or expose GeneticAlgorithmEngine from row 9 in multi-objective mode)
replacements.customer_claim: Show all reasonable trade-offs, not just one 'optimal' — customer picks

replacements.old: yield = P(all tolerances met) — Monte Carlo correct
replacements.replacement: Confirmed Monte Carlo: sample N=10⁴ realizations of each tolerance contribution from N(μ_i, σ_i²), check all spec limits, yield = fraction passing. Use quasi-MC (Sobol sequence) for 10–100× variance reduction. Cpk approximation valid only for single-feature univariate.
replacements.engine: EXISTING MonteCarloEngine + ToleranceStackEngine
replacements.customer_claim: Realistic yield % including all feature interactions

replacements.old: Sample plan from AQL — table lookup
replacements.replacement: Frame as RULE: GD&T type (position/profile/runout) → sampling strategy. Position → 4 datum-targets + N feature-points (N from Hopp criterion). Profile → 7+ points per feature. Runout → 360° scan at min 6 stations. Combine with Cpk-based n* = (z·σ/Δ)².
replacements.engine: EXISTING ProbingEngine + NEW InspectionPlanEngine
replacements.customer_claim: CMM-routine auto-generated from print, statistically valid

replacements.old: Cpk > 1.33 → ramp — correct decision rule
replacements.replacement: Confirmed Cpk gate; ADD prediction-interval lower-bound (Bayesian): with n samples, P(true Cpk ≥ 1.33 | observed) > 95% before ramping. Small-sample Cpk has wide CI — need n ≥ 30 for tight estimate.
replacements.engine: EXISTING CpkEngine; expose Bayesian-CI mode
replacements.customer_claim: Statistical confidence in Cpk before betting production run — not just point estimate

replacements.old: Check axis-travel-limits — boolean
replacements.replacement: Forward-kinematics envelope check: for each block, compute tool-tip + holder + spindle positions, intersect with machine envelope polytope. Plus collision-check vs fixture mesh. Output: safe / collision-at-block-N / out-of-travel-axis-X.
replacements.engine: EXISTING KinematicsEngine + CollisionDetectionEngine
replacements.customer_claim: Pre-flight G-code safety check — catch travel/collision before crash

replacements.old: t_actual = t_predicted · α_skill — empirical fudge
replacements.replacement: Learning curve (Wright): t_n = t_1·n^(log₂(LR)) where LR ∈ [0.7, 0.95] learning rate. After N repetitions, asymptote at t_∞ ≈ t_predicted·(1 + δ_machine). Track per-operator LR from historical data; calibrate predictions.
replacements.engine: NEW OperatorLearningCurveEngine
replacements.customer_claim: Realistic cycle for THIS operator, not theoretical robot

replacements.old: alarm if P > P_baseline + 3σ — fixed threshold
replacements.replacement: Adaptive: One-class SVM or Isolation Forest on (V, f, ap, material) features → P_predicted_distribution; alarm when observed P falls in <1st percentile. Catches process-shift (dull tool, wrong material, miscalibrated) not just over-power.
replacements.engine: NEW AnomalyDetectionEngine (Isolation Forest or OC-SVM)
replacements.customer_claim: Catch subtle process drift before it scraps parts

replacements.old: u_total = √(Σu_i²) — RSS
replacements.replacement: GUM-compliant uncertainty propagation: u_y² = Σ(∂f/∂x_i)²·u(x_i)² + 2·ΣΣ(∂f/∂x_i)(∂f/∂x_j)·u(x_i,x_j) (correlation terms). For nonlinear f: Monte Carlo propagation (10⁴ samples). Coverage k=2 for 95%. Output uncertainty budget identifying dominant contributor.
replacements.engine: NEW UncertaintyPropagationEngine — orchestrates all upstream engines
replacements.customer_claim: Quantified end-to-end uncertainty with dominant-source attribution — actionable improvement target

F-r3-a5-A.issue: Rows 1, 2, 6 had non-trivial physics errors that propagated through any downstream composition. Original V7.B treated 'combinatoric' as 'orthogonal', which only holds when each row introduces a legitimately new variability axis. After forensic rewrite, 27 of 50 rows now compose existing engines correctly; 23 require new engines.
F-r3-a5-A.remediation: Build 23 new engines per spec above; reframe rows 22, 25, 26, 45 as DATA SURFACES / RULES not EQUATIONS

F-r3-a5-B.issue: Rows 9 (cycle-time) and 43 (Pareto) were claimed convex/grid-search — both are non-convex MINLP requiring metaheuristics. Honest claim is 'best-found ± stderr over 30 restarts', not 'optimal'.
F-r3-a5-B.remediation: Add explicit disclaimer to customer claims; SimulatedAnnealingEngine + GeneticAlgorithmEngine

F-r3-a5-C.issue: Row 10 (Conformal) symmetric form gives marginal coverage only; asymmetric heteroscedastic regimes (most manufacturing) need CQR. Round-2 NN-CONFORMAL03 already shipped this — wire it.
F-r3-a5-C.remediation: Reference existing ConformalCalibrationEngine.predictAdaptiveIntervals() — no new build, just correct attribution

F-r3-a5-D.issue: Row 3 (ChatterStability) confirmed Round-2 F-r2-a3-B finding: Altintas oriented-FRF method must use Φ_oriented(jω), not stiffness scalar. Single-mode tap-test rep insufficient; multi-mode extraction required.
F-r3-a5-D.remediation: Verify ChatterStabilityEngine implements multi-mode FRF synthesis; add tap-test ingestion pipeline

F-r3-a5-E.issue: Rows 22 (insert-grade lookup), 25 (material-DB), 26 (WEDM-feasibility classifier), 45 (GD&T inspection plan) were framed as 'equations' but are RULES/DATA-SURFACES. Customer-facing claim should not promise 'physics-derived' for these.
F-r3-a5-E.remediation: Reframe in customer copy as 'expert-system rules validated by physics'
